questions.q: What determines the exact price of gas at any given moment, per this lesson?
options: Supply, demand, and network capacity
The price of Bitcoin
A fixed rate set once by Vitalik Buterin
The number of validators worldwide, which never changes
questions.explain: Gas price moves with how busy the network is — the more demand for block space relative to capacity, the higher gas prices climb.

questions.q: What is the real formula for calculating a gas fee, since Ethereum's August 2021 update?
options: Units of gas used × (base fee + priority fee)
Ether price × 21,000
A flat $5 per transaction
Units of gas used ÷ base fee
questions.explain: The gas fee is the amount of gas the transaction consumes, multiplied by the base fee (set by the network) plus any priority fee (a tip to the validator).

questions.q: Which unit is 10⁻⁹ (a billionth) of one ether, and is commonly used to quote gas prices?
options: Gwei
Wei
Finney
Satoshi
questions.explain: Gwei (giga-wei) equals 10⁻⁹ ETH and is the standard unit gas prices are quoted in — wei is even smaller, at 10⁻¹⁸ ETH.

questions.q: What real change happened to Ethereum's consensus mechanism in September 2022?
options: It switched from proof of work to proof of stake
It switched from proof of stake to proof of work
Gas fees were permanently eliminated
Ethereum merged with Bitcoin
questions.explain: Ethereum moved from proof of work (miners solving math problems) to proof of stake (validators staking ETH), after which a portion of gas fees became a staking reward.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what are two real ways to reduce how much you pay in gas fees?
options: Time transactions for low-traffic periods, and use Layer 2 solutions
Always use the highest possible priority fee
Only transact on weekends, which is the only factor that matters
There is no way to reduce gas fees
questions.explain: Choosing off-peak times (using a tool like Etherscan's gas tracker) and moving activity to Layer 2 networks are the two real strategies covered in class.
